name: TMUA
description: A short, mixed-topic path through mathematical thinking and reasoning. Later lessons deliberately revisit earlier ideas.

lessons.title: Implications and reverses
lessons.description: Read implications carefully and spot a tempting but invalid reverse.

lessons.title: Proof moves
lessons.description: Choose a useful proof strategy and state its key step.

lessons.title: Surds and patterns

lessons.title: Mixed retrieval

questions.prompt: What is the contrapositive of P implies Q?
questions.explanation: Reverse the order and negate both statements. An implication and its contrapositive are logically equivalent.

questions.prompt: Fill in the missing word: If passing an exam guarantees entry to a course, then passing is a [missing word] condition for entry.
questions.explanation: A sufficient condition guarantees the outcome: passing implies entry.
questions.answerInstruction: Type the missing word (one word), not the full phrase.

questions.prompt: All multiples of 4 are even. A number is even, so a student concludes it must be a multiple of 4. Name the error.
questions.explanation: From P implies Q and Q, one cannot conclude P. For example, 6 is even but is not a multiple of 4.

questions.prompt: What is enough to disprove a claim that a statement is true for every integer?

acceptedAnswers: one example where it is false
a case where it is false

questions.explanation: A universal claim fails as soon as a single case makes it false.
questions.answerInstruction: Type a short phrase naming one counterexample.

questions.prompt: In the inductive step, what implication do you prove?
questions.explanation: Assume the statement holds for k, then prove it holds for k + 1. Together with a base case, this establishes the result for all relevant integers.
questions.answerInstruction: Enter an implication linking the statement for k with the statement for k + 1.

questions.prompt: In a proof by contradiction, what do you assume first?

options.text: The statement you want to prove is false
The statement is true for one random example

questions.explanation: Assume the negation of the claim and derive an impossibility; that contradiction shows the negation cannot hold.
Write 72 as 36 times 2, then take the square root of the perfect square 36.
Multiply each term: x squared minus 3x plus 2x minus 6, which simplifies to x squared minus x minus 6.
